local.profile: official Appwrite 1.9.6 self-host Docker Compose stack

hosted.gapReason: No arm-scoped Appwrite Cloud target or credentials were provided; not scored as a product failure.

assistanceEvents.detail: Used current official Appwrite self-host, TablesDB transaction/permission, Realtime, Storage, Function, variable, scheduler, and execution documentation.

commands.classification: environment-prerequisite: No Docker-compatible runtime, passwordless sudo, or usable rootless namespace support. Resolution: Coordinator reassigned this arm to an isolated local control-plane target.

installer-stream-termination: Official installer SSE terminated after the exact stack was already healthy; Colima did not mirror /private/tmp bind outputs. Resolution: Readiness-gated recovery copied generated Compose files from the exact installer container.

control-plane-network-and-function-key: Colima runtime could not reach a macOS-hosted sink, and the generated execution key did not authorize the TablesDB write at the external API endpoint. Resolution: Placed an arm-owned sink on the isolated runtimes network and configured the arm API key as a secret function variable.

realtime-subscription-ergonomics: Concurrent and array multi-channel subscribe patterns failed to observe later wall/guest channels; collection delivery also required table-level read authority. Resolution: Awaited subscriptions sequentially and modeled visibility/revocation with explicit table permission transitions.

local-scheduler-latency: Cron scheduler loaded and enqueued the function, but the execution was not inspectable inside the bounded harness wait. Resolution: Used Appwrite's native future scheduledAt execution API with minute precision.

auth-subscription-race-and-client-rate-limit: A fresh browser raced anonymous Realtime registration with Auth restoration; repeated client-session burst writes also reached endpoint rate limiting. Resolution: Subscribed only after Auth and used native server batch createRows for each exact 20-row burst.

provider-runtime-residue-and-probe-bug: Compose cleanup left three exact project-named Open Runtimes containers, while docker inspect of the absent sink returned an empty JSON array on stdout despite failure. Resolution: Validated runtime name/ID/type/image before removal, changed the sink probe to use exit status, and added an Open Runtimes negative probe.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: The exact frozen fixture and three native Auth principals were independently counted through Appwrite authority.
Anonymous reads returned public preview rows only; private fields live in a separately permissioned table.
Bob's native session exercised yes/maybe/no plus-one transitions and admin authority verified every settlement.
Host, cohost, guest, and outsider exercised distinct positive and negative authority paths.
Guest-list permission transitioned independently of public preview; an already-connected client received no protected update.
Two actor-scoped native transactions raced for the final seat; Appwrite committed one and rejected one with conflict.
A second browser client observed the frozen 20-post burst and RSVP-total transition over Appwrite Realtime.
Authenticated upload, actor-specific delivery, exact content hash, and post-delete negative proof used Appwrite Storage.
Appwrite's scheduled-execution API invoked the deployed function at a declared future time; its run and deduplicated attempt are inspectable.
The deployed Function crossed a secret-authenticated effect boundary twice while the unique dedupe ledger retained one delivery.
A sink-side commit followed by socket destruction remained explicitly ambiguous; retry learned duplicate success without a second effect.
Revocation stopped future protected reads and Realtime delivery; the UI honestly retained previously authorized in-memory data until refresh.

scenarioResults.note: Local Appwrite Function deployment, secret configuration, logs, and effects are inspectable; hosted evidence is an environment/credential GAP.

actor-authority.reason: Three native Auth sessions directly prove host, cohost, invited guest, and outsider positive/negative authority.

transaction-conflict.reason: Two actor transactions race at 49/50; exactly one commits and one returns native 409 while authority remains 50.

transport.reason: A persistent independent browser observes the exact 20-post/RSVP burst over native Appwrite Realtime, with seven latency samples.

offline-reconnect.reason: Revocation directly inspected the already-connected client's retained in-memory data, but the frozen Partiful app has no persistent browser-offline scenario and no durable offline row store was claimed.

settlement.reason: RSVP transitions, the final-seat conflict, exact asset lifecycle, scheduled execution, and both known-success and ambiguous effect retries reached independently inspected authoritative settlements.

target-identity.reason: Version, hashed endpoint/project/config, native counts/indexes/function/storage, and exact Compose resources bind the target.

cleanup-isolation.reason: Empty baseline, exact path/project/name/PID guards, and post-cleanup negative probes prove isolated retirement.

artifact-reproducibility.reason: Pinned dependencies and installer, provisioning, function, UI, tests, performance, audit, inventory, and cleanup source are retained.
